speaker: Doctor
text: To begin our assessment of your breast mass, have you noticed any changes in size, shape, or skin texture over the last few months? Additionally, have you experienced any nipple discharge, pain, or lumps in the underarm area? Please also tell me your age and if you have a family history of breast cancer.

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given the rapid growth over just four weeks, have you noticed any skin dimpling, redness, warmth, or changes to the nipple itself, such as inversion or discharge? Also, do you have any fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying those symptoms. Since the mass is growing rapidly but lacks inflammatory signs like redness or fever, I need to check your vital signs and blood work to rule out infection or systemic issues. REQUEST TEST: CBC and CRP. REQUEST TEST: Serum_lactate_dehydrogenase. Do you have any history of trauma to the left breast or recent childbirth?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No family history of breast cancer. Social history: Non-smoker, moderate alcohol use. Elementary school teacher.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, night sweats, or changes in appetite. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: It appears there may have been a misunderstanding, as gastroenteritis does not present with a rapidly growing breast mass; this requires immediate clarification. Can you confirm if you have any history of trauma to the left breast, and would you be willing to undergo an ultrasound to evaluate the nature of this lesion? REQUEST IMAGES: Breast_Ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Mammography.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mammography Findings: Smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast. Biopsy Microscopic Description: Image shows leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes Tumor. The rapid growth of the mass combined with the mammographic finding of a polylobulated shape and the biopsy showing leaf-like structures with stromal overgrowth is classic for this diagnosis. I recommend immediate surgical excision to prevent recurrence or malignant transformation.
